question: Which of the following is true about the Zaid season in Indian agriculture?

options.text: It begins with the onset of winter.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It follows the Rabi season.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Zaid season:-**

 
 
• The Zaid season is also known as the summer or intermediate crop season in Indian agriculture.
 
• It typically starts in June and ends in September.
 
• It is characterized by high temperatures and occasional rainfall, which makes it suitable for crops that require less water, such as vegetables, fruits, and pulses.
 
• Zaid season follows the Rabi season, which ends in March/April, and precedes the Kharif season, which starts in June/July.
